chunks: As for the infidels, (it will be said): 'Were not My messages read out to you? But you behaved with self-conceit, and became a sinful people.'

key_terms.الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: The disbelievers / those who rejected faith
key_terms.فَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ: So you became arrogant / behaved with self-conceit
key_terms.قَوْمًا مُجْرِمِينَ: A sinful people / a people of criminals

ai.seo_question: Why did the disbelievers reject the Quranic messages despite them being recited to them?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the causal link between intellectual arrogance (istikbar) and moral corruption, illustrating how the rejection of divine signs (ayat) leads to a state of persistent transgression. It serves as a warning that mere exposure to revelation is insufficient without humility, a theme central to the concept of 'Aql (intellect) in Shia theology.
